this_week.title: New risk: The fuel is at its record and has not started to burn
this_week.why: The heat that will surface later is already piled up under the equator, and it is at a record for the whole series. This is measured, not forecast: the surface has not yet shown what is already stored below. While the gauge is not falling, the event has something to grow on.

this_week.title: New risk: The air is answering the ocean, so the event can travel
this_week.why: El Niño is not a warm patch of water, it is a coupling: the water heats, the trade winds give way, the cloud tower moves east, and only then does the event reach harvests on the other side of the planet. All three are in place now, which is why the regional impacts on this page a

this_week.title: New risk: The atmosphere is still catching up, by three floors
this_week.why: The ocean heats the air, not the other way round, and the air takes months to answer. That is why the warmest months of the whole record usually arrive AFTER the peak of an El Niño, not during it — and why the year that follows this one is the one to watch.

this_week.title: New risk: Water +11.3 °C above normal is sitting at 100 m under 125°W
this_week.why: This is the heat that has not surfaced yet. It is measured directly, every day, and it is what makes 'the event has room to grow' a statement about the present rather than about the past events.

this_week.title: New risk: The upper 300 m of the central and eastern Pacific hold +2.51 °C of extra heat
this_week.why: The CPC calls this the upper-ocean heat content index and watches it as the leading sign of where the surface goes next. A whole degree across that band is a large charge.

this_week.title: New risk: Global temperature in 2027 is likely to run above 2026; regional impacts follow their own lags
this_week.why: The dashboard measures the ocean today, but people meet an El Niño through harvests, water and prices, and those arrive with a delay of six to eighteen months. The plans that matter are for next year: import contracts, reserves, water rationing, insurance.

this_week.title: New risk: 2 westerly wind bursts in the last 120 days, the latest 13 days ago
this_week.why: Bursts are how an El Niño is fed: the warm water each one sends east surfaces off South America two to three months later. The bursts of the last four months are the ones arriving now and through the autumn.

this_week.title: New risk: The ocean holds more heat than ever measured (0–2000 m)
this_week.why: This is the reservoir the event draws on and returns to. A record reservoir means the statistical forecasts, trained on a cooler ocean, are reading a different system than the one they learned.

this_week.title: New risk: A very strong El Niño is under way
this_week.why: Water in the key patch of the Pacific is 2.6 degrees warmer than normal. The threshold for a “very strong” event is two degrees. This is not a forecast, it is already measured, and it has never happened this early in the year.

this_week.title: New risk: The event has room to grow: the fuel is charged and the analogues peaked in winter
this_week.why: Every past event of this strength peaked in winter, November to January. It is the end of summer now, so two or three more months of growth are likely. How much higher cannot be said: we are already above anything the ocean has shown at this time of year, and past events are no g

this_week.title: New risk: The eastern Pacific is heating, off the coast of South America
this_week.why: There are two kinds of El Niño: one heats the middle of the ocean, the other the east, off Peru and Ecuador. This is the second kind, the harshest in its consequences: 1982 and 1997 were like this. Such events brought downpours and floods to the coast of South America and drought

this_week.title: New risk: The world ocean is warmer every day than it has ever been on that day
this_week.why: On each of the last 30 days the ocean, averaged over the planet, was warmer than on the same day of any year since 1982. Not one hot day, but an unbroken stretch.

this_week.title: New risk: Niño 3.4: not a spike but a new level
this_week.why: The series did not jump and come back; it rose and stayed. The gauge that accumulates the excess over the spring level crossed its threshold 94 days ago and has only grown since.

this_week.title: New risk: world ocean: not a spike but a new level
this_week.why: The series did not jump and come back; it rose and stayed. The gauge that accumulates the excess over the spring level crossed its threshold 60 days ago and has only grown since.

this_week.title: New risk: land+ocean: not a spike but a new level
this_week.why: The series did not jump and come back; it rose and stayed. The gauge that accumulates the excess over the spring level crossed its threshold 33 days ago and has only grown since.

this_week.title: New risk: world ocean: the last 30 days are the warmest in the whole record
this_week.why: For these same dates none of the 45 years was warmer. Even after subtracting the general warming, +0.33 degrees remain above it: that is what the event itself adds.

watch: The key patch of the Pacific crossing the analogue median 2.881 or the 90th forecast edge 3.102, because that would mean it is outpacing the analogue path.
The water at 125°W, 100 m depth moving above 11.27 °C, or the warm water volume dropping from its record share without discharging, which would signal how much fuel remains.
A new westerly wind burst in the next two weeks: the last burst ended 2026-08-21 and active_now is false, with the MJO in phase 3 at amplitude 1.19 and not in the burst window.
The next IRI issue raising the combined peak above 3.25 or increasing the 10 of 26 models that are already below reality.
The easternmost Pacific index Niño 1+2 staying near 4.2 °C and crossing its historical maximum 4.5, which would mean the eastern warming continues.
